title: Nocturne in E-flat major
hook: Opening statement of the Nocturne: B-flat pickup, then bars 1-4 (G-F-G-F-E-flat-B-flat, the C-turn-C-G-B-flat-A-flat-G rise, F-G-D-E-flat-C-B-flat, the D-C-B-flat-A-flat-G-A-flat descent and the cadence on the held E-flat before the rest)

evidence.summary: Mutopia piece 1590 (G. Schirmer 1881, LilyPond source and PDF, SHA-256 3ff1dda16c3c39896355505ceb95d34c6307aaf9f713f6b0f530eee2526a2bf7) upper staff events 0-28; the printed PDF page 1 was read directly: pickup Bb, bars 1-4 and the turn sign of bar 2 (finger 12121, flat above, natural below = C Db C B C), phrase ending "ef4. r4" before the next pickup. The derivative realises the turn with the grid of bitmidi 28233 RIGHT HAND events 0-32, which matches all 33 pitches and every onset exactly (ticks/PPQ). Mutopia MIDI plus score are one source; bitmidi 28233 is independently sequenced (PPQ 48, rubato tempo map, ornament written out).

title: The Tide Is High
hook: Chorus of The Tide Is High (Atomic Kitten version): the high G-E-D-C descent with the D-E rise, the E-D-C-B-C-D-D-E answer, and the last line G-G-F-E-F-G

evidence.summary: bitmidi 8215 (Atomic Kitten version, key of C, 104 BPM) track 17 events 31-50, four legato tails of at most 29 ms closed in a derivative, compared event by event with a direct transcription of the public Hooktheory Atomic Kitten chorus (hash nLganLzlxYp, synced to the official video 1w2kaQUNLNY): all 20 pitches equal after one octave shift, onsets within 0.25 beat. Third sources: bitmidi 102722 (Blondie arrangement, quantized) and bitmidi 18319 (oboe, 18 attacks) agree on every pitch they contain.

title: The Next Episode
hook: The instrumental riff of The Next Episode, one complete 12-attack cycle (two bars): A-E-E-D-E-D-C-D-D-C-A-C in the MIDI key (D#-A#-A#-G#-A#-G#-F#-G#-G#-F#-D#-F# in the recording key D# minor)

evidence.summary: dre-nextepisode-fm.mid track 16 (lead, program 81) events 17-28 compared event by event with the Hooktheory public TheoryTab "The Next Episode" intro (notes 0-11 of 48, D# minor, 94 BPM): all 12 pitches agree after one constant +6 and all 12 onsets are exact. Both sources state the riff four times (midi events 17-64, tab notes 0-47) with identical interval and onset patterns. Recognizability metrics: 4 distinct pitches, repeated-attack share 0.182, longest repeated run 2; no listening review.
